description: RFC 8785 (JCS) vectors for amq.remote.link/1. Each vector is a JSON text (input) and either its canonical form (canonical, and canonical_hex for the exact UTF-8 bytes) or refused: true. Profile: integers only within +-(2^53-1) (a fraction, an exponent or a larger integer is refused, never formatted), at most 64 nested objects and arrays; duplicate keys, lone surrogates and trailing data are refused. RFC 8785 Appendix A is not a vector: it has fractions. Generated by a JSON.parse/sort/JSON.stringify oracle independent of the Go canonicalizer; internal/remote/jcs reproduces every vector.

vectors.name: case-colliding-keys
vectors.note: Keys that differ only by case are distinct and sort by UTF-16 code units (uppercase first). A strict consent decoder refuses such a pair; JCS itself does not.

vectors.name: html-characters
vectors.note: < > & are written as they are. Go encoding/json escapes them by default; JCS does not.

vectors.name: line-separator
vectors.note: U+2028 and U+2029 are written as raw UTF-8, never escaped.

vectors.name: non-bmp-character
vectors.note: A surrogate pair is one character, written as 4-byte UTF-8.

vectors.name: non-bmp-key-order
vectors.note: U+1F600 (UTF-16 D83D DE00) sorts before U+E000; code-point order would put U+E000 first.

vectors.name: control-characters
vectors.note: C0 controls use the short escapes where JSON has one and \u00xx (lowercase) otherwise; the solidus is not escaped.

vectors.name: raw-non-ascii
vectors.note: Non-ASCII, DEL and a literal U+FFFD are written as they are.

vectors.name: integers
vectors.note: The integer profile: -0 becomes 0; +-(2^53-1) is the largest magnitude.

vectors.name: structure-and-whitespace
vectors.note: Whitespace is dropped; nested objects are sorted too.

vectors.name: rfc8785-3.2.3-key-order
vectors.input: {"\u20ac":"Euro Sign","\r":"Carriage Return","\u000a":"Newline","1":"One","\u0080":"Control\u007f","\ud83d\ude02":"Smiley","\u00f6":"Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis","\ufb33":"Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh"}
vectors.canonical: {"\n":"Newline","\r":"Carriage Return","1":"One","":"Control","ö":"Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis","€":"Euro Sign","😂":"Smiley","דּ":"Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh"}
vectors.note: RFC 8785 section 3.2.3: keys sort by UTF-16 code units: "\n" "\r" "1" "\u0080" "ö" "€" "😂" "דּ".

vectors.name: rfc8785-3.2.2.2-string
vectors.note: RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.2: the string example. (Appendix A cannot be a vector: it has fractions, outside the integer profile.)

vectors.name: depth-64
vectors.note: 64 nested arrays: the deepest document accepted.

vectors.name: depth-65
vectors.note: 65 nested objects and arrays are refused.

vectors.name: lone-high-surrogate
vectors.note: A lone surrogate has no UTF-16 form to sort or hash by.

vectors.name: lone-low-surrogate
vectors.note: A lone low surrogate.

vectors.name: reversed-surrogate-pair
vectors.note: Low before high is two lone surrogates.

vectors.name: duplicate-key
vectors.note: Duplicate keys are refused, never last-wins.

vectors.name: integer-above-safe-range
vectors.note: 2^53 is outside the integer profile.

vectors.name: fraction
vectors.note: Fractions are outside the integer profile.

vectors.name: exponent
vectors.note: Exponents are outside the integer profile, even when the value is an integer.

vectors.name: trailing-data
vectors.note: One JSON text only.
